questions.q: You add three field filters to a report and never set filter logic. How are the filters combined?
options: With OR, so a record needs to match only one
With AND, so a record must match all three
Only the first filter is applied
The builder asks you to pick at run time
questions.explain: By default the numbered field filters are joined with AND, like a chain of AND conditions in a WHERE clause.

questions.q: You want records that match filter 1 and also match either filter 2 or filter 3. Which filter logic is correct?
options: 1 OR 2 AND 3
1 AND 2 OR 3
(1 AND 2) OR 3
1 AND (2 OR 3)
questions.explain: Parentheses group the OR so that filter 1 is required in every case. Mixing AND and OR without parentheses is easy to get wrong.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT belong inside your numbered filter-logic expression in most orgs?
options: A field filter on Amount
A field filter on Lead Source
A cross filter (for example, Accounts with Opportunities)
A field filter on Probability
questions.explain: Cross filters, like the standard Show Me and date filters, sit outside the numbered field-filter expression and are combined with AND.

questions.q: What does the Locked checkbox on a report filter do?
options: Prevents the report from being edited by anyone, including its owner
Stops people who run the report from changing that filter
Encrypts the filtered field values
Hides the filter from the report entirely
questions.explain: A locked filter shows a padlock and cannot be changed by viewers running the report, though they can still add their own filters.

questions.q: You need Stage equals Prospecting OR Qualification, all on one picklist field. What is often the simplest approach?
options: Write filter logic with two separate filters
Use a cross filter
List both values in a single filter on that field
Build a bucket column
questions.explain: A picklist filter accepts multiple values and treats them like an IN list, so no filter logic is needed for a one-field OR.
